Table II-11 presents a summary of coal mining within a 100-mile radius of the Westmoreland leases. The Decker and Rosebud coal mines plan substantial increases in production over the next few years. An EIS for the new Decker mines is being prepared by the Montana Department of State Lands and the Department of Interior. All these mines are surface operations, and all are working subbituminous coal in the Tongue River Formation, with the exception of the Divide coal mine which works a bituminous bed in the Bull Mountains south of Roundup, Montana. Oil and Gas - The Hardin gas field is the only producing field within about 30 miles of the Project Area. Oil is still being produced from the Snyder field, a few miles to the west of Tract II in T. 1 N., R. 35 E., west of Tullock Creek. Exploration for oil and gas is occurring on the Crow Indian Reservation, but no production has resulted. Other Minerals - The Fort Union Formation, which forms the bedrock for the entire area of both lease tracts, is not presently a source of metallic or non-metallic resources other than coal. Some mudstone of the Fort Union has bloating qualities when heated, and might be used for the production of light-weight aggregate, but other sources provide better quality raw material and there is no source of local demand (Mapel, 1975). Development of this potential resource is unlikely.
The alluvial deposits of Sarpy Creek and Tullock Creek constitute a possible source of road surfacing material. Clinker also has been used extensively as a source of road surfacing material.
